title: 第十八章复仇第十九章入局第二十章寻刀
lines: 第十八章复仇
宋焘抱着天书，走了很多天。他不知道自己要去哪里，只知道不能再看了。但他还是打开了天书。不是他想看，是天书自己翻开的。
这一章，叫《商三官》。
诸城有个书生，叫商士禹。此人性格刚直，最看不惯豪强欺压百姓。元宵节那天，他去街上赏灯，看见本县豪绅王半城在街上横行霸道，强抢民女。商士禹上前阻拦，被王半城的家丁打了一顿。他气不过，写了状子去告官。王半城买通了县令，反告商士禹诬陷好人，判了他一个“诽谤之罪”，重杖四十，遣返回家。
商士禹被打得皮开肉绽，抬回家中，没几天就死了。他死的时候，两个儿子跪在床前哭，女儿商三官站在门口，没有哭。她只是看着父亲的脸，看了很久。
商士禹死后，两个哥哥去告状。告了一年，官司输了。又告了一年，还是输了。王半城有钱有势，县令是他的人，知府是他的人。两个哥哥告得倾家荡产，连路费都拿不出来了。他们对三官说：“妹妹，告不赢了。算了吧。”
三官说：“你们去办丧事吧。官司的事，不用你们管了。”
两个哥哥以为她说气话，没有放在心上。他们给父亲办了丧事，把棺材停在屋里，等官司打赢了再下葬。但他们知道，官司赢不了了。他们放弃了。
三官没有放弃。她把自己关在屋里，三天没有出来。三天后，她出来了，穿了一身男装，剪了头发，脸上涂了锅灰，活脱脱一个少年书生的模样。她对两个哥哥说：“我出去走走。你们别找我。”
两个哥哥拦不住她。她走了，再也没有回来。
三官走了很多地方。她打听到王半城喜欢看戏，便去学戏。她天生一副好嗓子，又肯下功夫，半年就学会了十几出戏。她给自己取了个艺名，叫“李玉”。
她辗转到了王半城所在的县城，混进了一个戏班子。班主看她生得俊俏，唱得好，很是喜欢。没过多久，王半城过寿，请戏班子去家里唱堂会。三官跟着班子去了。
王半城坐在堂上，翘着二郎腿，看着台上的戏。三官扮的是花旦，一出场，王半城的眼睛就亮了。他问班主：“那个小生是谁？”
班主说：“新来的，叫李玉。”
王半城点了点头，没有说话。戏唱完了，王半城让管家把三官叫到跟前。他上下打量她，越看越喜欢。
“你多大了？”他问。
“十八。”三官的声音很低。
“留下来吧。”王半城说，“在我府里唱戏，亏待不了你。”
三官低着头，没有说话。她点了点头。
当天夜里，三官住进了王半城的府里。王半城让她住在自己的书房旁边，好吃好喝地供着。三官很安静，不爱说话，也不爱笑。王半城问她什么，她就答什么，不多一个字。王半城以为她是害羞，没有在意。
三官在王半城府里住了半个月。半个月里，她把府里的地形摸得一清二楚——王半城住在哪间房，夜里几个人守门，什么时候睡得最沉。她都知道了。
这天夜里，王半城喝醉了酒，回到房里。他让人把三官叫来，说要听她唱戏。三官来了，手里端着一壶茶。她给王半城倒了一杯茶，递过去。
“大人，喝杯茶醒醒酒。”
王半城接过茶碗，手碰到了她的手指。她的手指很凉，像一块玉。王半城笑了笑，握住她的手不放。
“李玉，你长得真好看。比女人还好看。”
三官没有说话。她把茶碗放在桌上，低下头，看着自己的手。王半城以为她害羞，笑得更厉害了。他松开她的手，端起茶碗喝了一口。茶很烫，他吹了吹，又喝了一口。
“李玉，你唱一段给我听。”
三官抬起头，看着他。她的眼睛很亮，很冷，像冬天的井水。
“大人想听什么？”
“随便。你唱什么我都喜欢。”
三官站起来，走到窗前，推开窗户。月光涌进来，照在她脸上。她的脸很白，很冷，像一块冰。她开口唱了。唱的是《窦娥冤》，唱到“地也，你不分好歹何为地；天也，你错勘贤愚枉做天”的时候，她的声音忽然变了，变得很尖，很厉，像刀锋划过铁器。
王半城听着，酒醒了一半。他看着她，忽然觉得有些不对。他正要开口问，三官转过身来，手里多了一把刀。刀很短，藏在袖子里，谁也没有发现。
content_en:
Chapter 18 Revenge
Song Tao walked for many days holding the Book of Heaven in his arms. He didn't know where he was going, he just knew he couldn't look any further. But he still opened the Book of Heaven. It’s not that he wanted to read it, it was the Book of Heaven that he opened by himself.
This chapter is called "Three Officials of Shang".
There was a scholar in Zhucheng named Shang Shiyu. This person has an upright character and dislikes the bullying of the people by powerful people. On the day of the Lantern Festival, he went to enjoy the lanterns on the street and saw Wang Bancheng, a wealthy gentleman from the county, running rampant on the street and robbing women of the people. Shang Shiyu stepped forward to stop him, but was beaten up by Wang Bancheng's servants. He was so angry that he wrote a complaint to the official. Wang Bancheng bribed the county magistrate, and counter-sued Shang Shiyu for falsely accusing a good person, and sentenced him to "defamation", gave him a forty-strong cane, and sent him home.
Shang Shiyu was beaten to pieces and was carried home. He died within a few days. When he died, his two sons knelt in front of the bed and cried, and his daughter Shang Sanguan stood at the door without crying. She just looked at her father's face for a long time.
After Shang Shiyu died, his two brothers went to complain. After a year of litigation, the lawsuit was lost. I sued for another year and still lost. Wang Bancheng is rich and powerful, the county magistrate is his person, and the prefect is his person. The two brothers sued so hard that they lost everything and couldn't even afford travel expenses. They said to the three officials: "Sister, you can't win if you sue. Forget it."
The third official said: "You go and hold the funeral. You don't have to worry about the lawsuit."
The two brothers thought she was speaking out of anger and didn't take it to heart. They held a funeral for their father and parked the coffin in the house until the lawsuit was won before burying him. But they knew they couldn't win the lawsuit. They gave up.
Sanguan did not give up. She locked herself in the house and didn't come out for three days. Three days later, she came out, dressed in men's clothes, with her hair cut and her face smeared with pot ash, looking exactly like a young scholar. She said to her two brothers: "I'm going out for a walk. Don't look for me."
The two brothers couldn't stop her. She left and never came back.
The three officials traveled to many places. She found out that Wang Bancheng liked going to the theater, so she went to learn opera. She was born with a good voice and was willing to work hard. She learned more than a dozen plays in half a year. She gave herself a stage name, "Li Yu".
She moved to the county where Wang Bancheng was located and got into a theater troupe. The class teacher liked her very much because she was pretty and could sing well. Not long after, Wang Bancheng celebrated his birthday and invited the opera troupe to sing at his home. The three officials followed the team.
Wang Bancheng sat in the hall with his legs crossed, watching the play on the stage. The three officials played the role of Hua Dan, and Wang Bancheng's eyes lit up as soon as he appeared. He asked the class teacher: "Who is that young student?"
The class leader said: "The new guy's name is Li Yu."
Wang Bancheng nodded and said nothing. After the play was over, Wang Bancheng asked the housekeeper to call the three officials. He looked her up and down, the more he looked at her, the more he liked her.
"How old are you?" he asked.
"Eighteen." The third official's voice was very low.
"Stay." Wang Bancheng said, "I won't treat you badly if you sing in my house."
The three officials lowered their heads and did not speak. She nodded.
That night, the three officials stayed in Wang Bancheng's house. Wang Bancheng let her live next to his study and provided her with delicious food and drinks. Sanguan is very quiet, doesn't like to talk or laugh. She answered whatever Wang Bancheng asked her, without adding a single word. Wang Bancheng thought she was shy and didn't pay attention.
The three officials stayed in Wang Bancheng's mansion for half a month. In half a month, she understood the topography of the house very clearly - which room Wang Bancheng lived in, how many people guarded the door at night, and when he slept the most deeply. She knew it all.
That night, Wang Bancheng returned to his room drunk. He asked the three officials to come over and said that he wanted to hear her sing an opera. The third official came with a pot of tea in his hand. She poured Wang Bancheng a cup of tea and handed it over.
"My lord, have a cup of tea to sober up."
Wang Bancheng took the tea bowl and touched her fingers with his hand. Her fingers were cold, like a piece of jade. Wang Bancheng smiled and held her hand.
"Li Yu, you are so beautiful. Even more beautiful than women."
The three officials did not speak. She put the tea bowl on the table, lowered her head, and looked at her hands. Wang Bancheng thought she was shy and laughed even harder. He let go of her hand, picked up the tea bowl and took a sip. The tea was very hot. He blew on it and took another sip.
"Li Yu, sing a piece for me."
The third officer raised his head and looked at him. Her eyes were bright and cold, like well water in winter.
"What do you want to hear, sir?"
"Whatever. I like whatever you sing."
Sanguan stood up, walked to the window, and opened the window. The moonlight poured in and shone on her face. Her face was very white and cold, like a piece of ice. She began to sing. She was singing "The Injustice of Dou E". When she sang "Earth, you don't distinguish between good and bad, what is earth? Heaven, you judge the virtuous and foolish in vain and make heaven in vain." Her voice suddenly changed, becoming very sharp and sharp, like a knife cutting through iron.
Wang Bancheng listened, half sober from the wine. He looked at her and suddenly felt something was wrong. Just as he was about to ask, Sanguan turned around with a knife in his hand. The knife was short and hidden in the sleeve, so no one noticed it.
